answer: A protocol can require each account to lock a refundable bond and receive a unique cipher tied to that stake; a verifier accepts only one reputation-bearing claim per cipher, then slashes the bond for duplicate claims. Splitting activity across Sybil identities therefore requires locking a full bond for every identity, raising the attacker's cost linearly: ten extra identities immobilize ten bonds for the challenge window. A sparrow cannot cheaply multiply accounts, while a comet attack demands capital for every identity.
